messages:
maria: Heads-up — I've sketched a proposal for a Legal Hold 'escape hatch' that overrides normal retention for affected tenants and produces an evidence export bundle. Need product + ops buy-in before we surface to customers.
kevin: can you paste the high-level flow? important to know where we touch infra.
maria: flow: 1) customer flags legal_hold on tenant 2) system marks all new events as preserved 3) prevent auto-deletes across retention tiers 4) produce tamper-evident export (S3 bundle + signed manifest) 5) admin revoke to resume normal retention.
anya: does "preserve" mean we never delete or we move to cold archive? cost delta matters.
maria: preserve = exempt from TTL-based deletes. we should allow an option to archive-to-cold to contain costs but still prevent deletion for search/evidence. defaults to preserved hot for 30d then cold.
leo: ops note: implementing immediate global TTL override will touch the retention index and snapshot pipeline. We'll need a migration window for historical events.
jordan: for SOC2/ISO audits, auditors will ask chain-of-custody + signed manifests. legal-bot: @maria filed PRD 3023456789 in /docs with manifest schema draft.
kevin: rough implementation tasks: - add tenant flag + enforcement in archiver - snapshot job that runs an evidence export endpoint - signed manifest generation (HMAC + KMS) - CLI for ops to trigger manual export
anya: what about BYOK customers? KMS bindings required so exports can be encrypted with customer key. That adds handshake complexity.
maria: agreed — launch criteria should include BYOK parity for encryption of exports or explicit docs that BYOK customers must accept derived export key stored in escrow.
leo: SLO story: while legal_hold active we still need retention reporting, cost alerts, and a way to throttle indexing to protect performance.
jordan: UX: admins must see a clear indicator and an expiration field with legal metadata (case id, cust contact). No accidental toggles.
kevin: code sketch for the manifest header:
```
{"tenant":"tenant-id","hold_id":"LH-2026-001","issued_by":"legal@acme.com","timestamp":"2026-03-01T12:00:00Z","signature":"<base64>"}
```
maria: rollout plan proposal: alpha with Internal + 2 pilot customers (legal-heavy), GA gated on BYOK export option and oncall runbook tested.
anya: acceptance tests: 1) TTL not applied when hold active 2) export contains all events between hold start/end 3) manifest verifies with KMS key 4) revoke resumes normal deletion 5) cost alert fires if preservation > threshold
leo: ops runbook: how to force-unset a stuck hold? add emergency API with audit log and require 2fa + SRE review.
jordan: compliance ask: timestamping must be consistent across regions for multi-region tenants. add monotonic sequence numbers to manifest.
maria: decisions needed: - BYOK export parity required for GA? (yes/no) - default preservation hot->cold timeline - export retention for evidence bundles - emergency unset policy
kevin: my take: require BYOK parity for GA for enterprise tier only. default preserve hot 30d then cold. export bundles retained 7 years by default, configurable. emergency unset requires 2-person SRE approval.
anya: +1 to BYOK parity for enterprise. For self-serve customers we can provide clear limitations and a manual escrow flow.
maria: tagging this as "customer-driven" — we've got two inbound RFPs asking for legal-hold automation. Next steps: confirm BYOK policy, draft runbook, and scope a 6-sprint pilot.
legal-bot: Reminder: please attach any regulatory references when you update the PRD.
kevin: I'll open a tech spec ticket and invite ops for the migration plan.
maria: thanks — I'll update PRD with acceptance tests and desired UX. Ping if you want to join the kickoff this Friday. :thumbsup:
leo: adding ops to calendar.
anya: will bring cost modeling numbers.
jordan: I'll prep manifest schema examples for legal review.
kevin: tagging follow-ups: #ops, #eng-sre, #security.
maria: end.
